elements.text: Failure of maintenance and inspection personnel to perform a proper inspection of the 7th stage high compressor disk
Allowing a detectable crack to grow to a critical length causing disk rupture
Disk rupture propelling engine fragments into the fuselage
Engine fragments severing the right engine main fuel line
Release of pressurized fuel inside the cabin
Sparks from steel fragments igniting fuel and causing a fire
Lack of an adequate recordkeeping system
Failure to use process sheets to document step-by-step overhaul/inspection procedures
Flightcrew met certification, training, and rest requirements
Flight attendants completed approved training program
Airplane was certificated and operated in accordance with regulations
Uncontained failure occurred at low airplane and high engine rotational speed
Fatigue crack in stress redistribution hole in the 7th stage high compressor disk
Detectable crack existed when the disk was overhauled in 1991
Disk did not receive a proper inspection during 1991 overhaul
THY repair station was not using process sheets at the time of overhaul
P&W JT8D engine manual lacked precise information, but this did not contribute to failure
FAA guidance on maintenance record detail is insufficient and vague
Recommendation for process sheets or similar documentation
Recommendation for foreign repair stations to be subject to FAA recordkeeping requirements
Industry practice of using serviceable tags without clear understanding
THY had authority under Part 145 to overhaul engines
Evacuation checklist item not completed due to smoke, but evacuation was successful
Pilot's delay in communication did not adversely affect evacuation
Deficiencies in flight attendant training did not affect occupant survivability
Regulation regarding lap children not always enforced
Flight attendant access to cockpit allowed quick notification
Aircraft did not meet current flammability standards, but this is a survival factor note
